newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed is Russia's most trusted politician - survey.
newsitem.headline: Lebed is Russia's most trusted politician - survey.

text.p: Russians trust outspoken security tsar Alexander Lebed much more than any other national politician, according to an opinion poll released on Thursday.

The poll by the respected VTsIOM research group, published in the liberal Sevodnya newspaper, showed that 40 percent of the people questioned had named Lebed among the five or six politicians they trusted most.
Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov was second with 16 percent, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin polled 14 percent and liberal leader Grigory Yavlinsky had 12 percent.

President Boris Yeltsin, who was re-elected by a big margin on July 3 but is now in a sanatorium awaiting heart surgery, was fifth on 11 percent. But this was much better than the five percent rating he received in a similar poll a year ago.
The poll of 2,430 people was carried out between September 6 and 29. They were asked: "Name the five or six politicians in Russia whom you trust most."
Opinion polls have not always proved accurate in Russia and Yeltsin's election victory showed how quickly poor ratings can be turned into good ones.

But the findings were sure to boost the morale of the reserve general who has not concealed his presidential ambitions since Yeltsin appointed him national security adviser as a reward for Lebed's third place in the presidential election.
The poll was conducted after Lebed signed a peace deal on August 31 which ended fighting in breakaway Chechnya, the major achievement of his almost four months in office.
It showed that people's trust in Lebed had more than doubled compared with a VTsIOM poll of September 1995 which showed Chernomyrdin was then the most trusted politician.
Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov, who is widely regarded as a potential presidential candidate, climbed into sixth place on seven percent compared with 12th place a year ago.
Ultra-nationalist Vladimir Zhirinovsky was in seventh place on five percent, the same rating as a year ago.
Lebed, Luzhkov and Chernomyrdin have been manoeuvring for position and influence in Yeltsin's absence.
A presidential election would be called early if Yeltsin proved unfit to govern. Doctors say the president is doing well and that his operation should go ahead in the next two months.
The table below shows how many percent of people polled named each politician among the five or six they most trusted.
Sept 1995 Sept 1996
Alexander Lebed 13 40
Gennady Zyuganov 11 16
Viktor Chernomyrdin 14 14
Grigory Yavlinsky 12 12
Boris Yeltsin 5 11
Yuri Luzhkov 3 7
Vladimir Zhirinovsky 5 5
